biggest_gap.what: Round 9's pelvis roll raised the whole figure relative to its own root, and nothing takes the rise back out. MEASURED THREE WAYS AND THEY AGREE. (1) On the built rig across the full 96-frame idle: the lower ankle rises a mean of 7.96 mm (min 7.1, max 8.87). (2) In the RUNNING GAME on an RTX A5000, at the flat player stand where ground = 2.680 m in both arms, the drawn ankles go from 0.0890 / 0.0901 m above ground to 0.0961 / 0.1012 m — +7.1 mm and +11.1 mm. (3) The sole is not the ankle: `game/src/render/actor.js` states its own measured geometry, that the skinned sole hangs 88 mm below the foot bone and clears the ground by 2 mm on the un-conformed NPC path. Applying that constant, the number of frames in the idle loop on which BOTH soles are clear of the ground goes from 24 of 96 to 68 of 96, and the largest gap under the lower sole goes from 2.0 mm to 10.9 mm. THE ROUND'S STATED REASON FOR NOT FIXING IT IS FALSE. Its status file says 'r7/r8's foot conform is designed to absorb exactly this... so it is plausibly absorbed'. It cannot be. `footConformDelta` is `clamp(groundAt(x,z) - groundY)` — a terrain DIFFERENCE term whose value on flat ground is exactly zero, which that same file calls 'the correct null, which a pin can never have', and which round 7 measured at 0.0000 m at all three F10 stands. A term that is identically zero cannot absorb a constant. The left/right foot difference on flat ground also got worse, not better: 0.0011 m -> 0.0052 m as drawn in the running game, and 0.00109 -> 0.00521 m across the loop on the rig.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every character in the game — the player and all 408 NPCs, because the change is on the single shared `idle_ready` layer — now stands about a centimetre above the floor for most of its idle loop instead of touching it, and the one system that could have hidden it is mathematically incapable of doing so on flat ground, which is where almost every NPC in every settlement stands.
biggest_gap.remedy: In `game/data/combat/clips.json`, take the rise back out where it was put in, NOT with a constant `root_offset` on `idle_loop` (the round is right that a constant there is a vertical step at the attack/idle boundary). Two buildable options, in preference order. (A) Add `idle_ready.root_offset.y = [[0,-0.0080],[3,-0.0080]]` — the stance layer is additive and already pinned at both ends by the termination rule, so a constant THERE is continuous by construction, which is exactly the property `root_offset` on the loop lacks. (B) If the additive layer's root offset is not consumed, reduce the free-leg knee bend from 8.248 deg to the value that levels the feet at 0.0900 rather than at 0.0989 by bisecting on the LOWER ankle's absolute height instead of on the left/right difference — the round solved the wrong objective, not with the wrong method. DONE means: `node tools/visual/f10-r9c-c3-audit.mjs` reports `B_feet.summary.rise_of_lower_ankle_m.mean` within 1 mm of 0 and `after.lr_diff_max_m` no worse than the before arm's 0.00109 m; `node tools/harness/anim-tune.mjs` still reports 0 of 14 over 0.35 m with worst `snapOut` <= 0.0122 m; and C3 still reads >= 2 of 3 over 3 deg at both frames.

secondary_observations.note: THE ROUND'S OWN PREDICTION, CONFIRMED BY LOOKING. Its status file says '3 degrees is the threshold at which a figure stops being provably a mannequin, not the threshold at which it starts looking like these'. I built the picture that settles it: our idle sampled at eight points across its own 96-frame loop, before above, after below, front and profile. The after row IS visibly asymmetric — one shoulder drops, the hip line lifts. It is also still a figure LEANING, not a figure with its weight on one leg: both legs remain vertical and parallel, the feet stay level and shoulder-width, the pelvis is not displaced laterally over a supporting leg, and the head stays centred over the middle of the stance. And the loop barely moves: the silhouette's minimum self-IoU against its own frame 0 is 0.9203 at the front (0.9675 before) and 0.9075 in profile (0.9115 before) — the profile did not change at all, because the weight shift is a roll and a roll is invisible from the side. The reference plates are a different order of magnitude: the ER Leyndell soldier's idle is yawed off-axis by tens of degrees and leaning on a wall, and the DS1 boss movesets transform their silhouette frame to frame. C3's 3 degrees is a floor, not a target, and the item's own provenance note already asks for it to be re-derived from `refs/characters/`. I did NOT change it — re-deriving a threshold from a measured population is a piece of work, not a critique (CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3, third guard).

The round recorded that `f10-r8-torso.mjs` 'HAS BEEN MEASURING THE TRUNK IN AN ATTACK POSE' because its default `pose: 'idle'` falls through `clips.archetypes['idle'] || Object.values(clips.archetypes)[0]` onto `cut_diagonal`. The fallback is real and `f10-silhouette.mjs` line 109 has it too, with the same default — so two of this item's instruments name one archetype and look up another. But evaluated on the built rig, `cut_diagonal@0` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to `idle_ready@0` on all twenty bones, in BOTH clip blobs: every non-looping archetype begins from the stand, which is what the termination rule is for. At phase 0 the fallback measures the idle after all, and my two `f10-silhouette` runs at `idle` and at `idle_ready` returned identical rosters to the pixel. It diverges the moment the phase is non-zero (`cut_diagonal@1.5` differs on 18 of 20 bones). So the trap is one key rename from biting and should be fixed — but a past number should not be discarded as 'mid-swing' without checking the phase it used. HAZARDS §20b.

Round 8 changed the saxhleel eye albedo 2.157x -> 0.847x, could not photograph it on valid hardware, and wrote that 'whether what replaced it READS as an eye at conversation distance on real hardware is not established'. Round 9 shot the eight FP frames that show it and did not open them. I opened all eight. THE CHANGE LANDED: sampled over the right eye patch, mean RGB goes (117.0, 93.6, 37.8) -> (86.9, 71.2, 38.5), a ~0.75x render-side ratio, in the expected direction. THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION IS NO. At 3x and 5x on the RTX A4500 close-up the eye is a flat amber lozenge pasted on the side of a smooth snout: no pupil of any kind, no iris/sclera division, no lid line, no orbit rim, no catchlight. It is darker paint, not an eye. Round 8's headgear change in the same frames IS a large and real improvement — the wide pale slab that spanned the whole skull at four of six bearings is gone and replaced by a slim band — but the band still floats clear of the cranium with visible background under it at bearing 000, and what it uncovered is a completely smooth brown egg.
